exposure: Maternal education (as a measure of early-life socioeconomic circumstances)
cohort: The study included 107,884 mother-child dyads from 7 European birth cohorts.
finding: Children from disadvantaged socioeconomic circumstances, indicated by lower maternal education, had a consistently increased risk of asthma (17%), partially mediated by early-life risk factors such as maternal smoking during pregnancy, adverse birth outcomes, and breastfeeding duration.
country: 6 European countries, including Denmark and France
followup_time: Up to 12 years (outcome assessed between 3-12 years of age)
